tagline: Down the grade to the Merced, on the first all-year road.
intro: Out of Mariposa, Highway 140 runs through Midpines with ponderosa pine on both sides, then takes a steep, winding grade down to the Merced River at Briceburg. From there it keeps to the river toward El Portal and the park, with the Sierra National Forest on the south bank and the Stanislaus on the north.

This is the All-Year Highway, built largely by prison labor and opened on July 31, 1926, on the south bank, opposite the Yosemite Valley Railroad. Visitor cars in the park nearly doubled the first year. The railroad ran its last scheduled train in 1945.

moments.title: Midpines
moments.text: Gold country first, the Whitlock district, with over 70 lode mines at its peak. In 1926, the year the highway opened, it started over as a resort.

moments.title: Briceburg
moments.text: Around 1924, 255 convicts camped here to build the highway up the canyon. When they left in 1926, William Brice moved his store across the river and the place took his name.

moments.title: Hites Cove
moments.text: Up the South Fork of the Merced lies the ghost town where John Hite struck a gold vein in 1861. The trail through the canyon is known for its spring wildflowers.
